title: Listing the hyperarithmetical functions
summary: Given a countable Turing ideal $\mathcal{I} \subseteq ω^ω$, we say that $x$ is a list (resp. weak list) of $\mathcal{I}$ if $\mathcal{I}=\{x^{[n]} : n \in ω\}$ (resp. if $\mathcal{I} \subseteq \{x^{[n]} :n \in ω\}$). We show that, for several natural ideals $\mathcal{I}$, $x$ computes a list of $\mathcal{I}$ if and only if it computes a function dominating all the functions in $\mathcal{I}$.
